question: Why Does 3D Secure (SCA) Authentication Keep Failing at Checkout?
metaDescription: Often a JavaScript conflict blocking the authentication popup or redirect, rather than the customer actually failing their bank's verification step.
shortAnswer: 3D Secure (the authentication step behind Strong Customer Authentication in the EU/UK) opens a popup or redirect from the customer's card issuer to verify the payment, and this extra layer is exactly where checkout page conflicts tend to surface — a popup blocker, a JavaScript error elsewhere on the page, or a theme/plugin interfering with the iframe can all break the flow before the customer ever gets a chance to actually authenticate.

bodyHtml:
Why This Happens

3D Secure works by opening a separate authentication frame or redirect from the card issuer's own systems, layered on top of the regular checkout flow. This is a more fragile integration point than a simple form submission — a JavaScript error anywhere else on the checkout page can prevent the popup script from firing at all, and some themes or security plugins interfere with iframes or popups by default, breaking the flow before the customer even reaches their bank's verification screen.

Common Causes

  • A JavaScript error elsewhere on the checkout page (from a theme, another plugin, or a tracking script) halting script execution before the 3D Secure handler can run.
  • Browser popup blockers if the integration uses a popup window rather than an inline iframe or redirect — some gateway integrations are more popup-blocker-resistant than others.
  • A security or firewall plugin blocking the issuer's authentication domain from loading in an iframe, mistaking it for a suspicious embed.
  • An outdated gateway plugin version not fully compliant with the latest 3D Secure 2 (SCA) specification, which has evolved since the original 3D Secure standard.
  • Genuine customer-side authentication failures (an actual wrong code entered, or their bank's app timing out) do happen too, and are worth ruling out by testing with a known-good test card first.

How to Fix It

  1. Check the browser console for JavaScript errors on the checkout page first, since this is the most common underlying cause.
  2. Test with popup blockers disabled to rule that out specifically.
  3. Update the gateway plugin to the latest version, confirming it explicitly supports 3D Secure 2 / SCA.
  4. Temporarily disable security/firewall plugins one at a time on a staging copy to isolate an iframe-blocking conflict.
  5. Test with the gateway's own known-good test card to confirm whether the underlying flow works at all outside of any theme/plugin conflict.
